item.description:
Aki 0.4.0

New

  • Marking leaves the app below alone, like the Mac's own ⌘⇧4: an open menu stays open, a selection stays selected.
  • The right session, by itself: mark a localhost:3001 page and your marks go to the session named "3001"; click an agent's tab in Orca and it becomes the destination.
  • Each mark's picture is copied: ⌘V pastes it anywhere (Settings turns it off).
  • Walk the screen with the arrows: ↑ ↓ ← → move to the next thing; ⇧↑ / ⇧↓ make it bigger or smaller; ⏎ marks it.
  • Messages your agent can trust: they say which session they're for, where the marks came from, and name them by code (aki show df9f68), so they work pasted into any terminal.
  • The queue in the History sends right there, and each mark's session can be changed.
  • A new sidebar: the AI's symbol in each ring, its state in a word, the destination framed. Drag a project by its name; sessions idle for two days tuck themselves into "+N".
  • Each mark has its own folder (~/.aki/marks/<day>/<code>/).

Fixed

  • Menus, drop-downs and Orca's own notices can be marked.
  • ↑ reaches the whole page; outlines stay inside the screen.
  • ⌘Tab works while marking; Aki's lists scroll.
  • A ring no longer spins for a session that's resting.
  • Clipboard histories (like Raycast's) show the copied picture.

item.title: 0.4.0-beta.36
item.description:
Aki 0.4.0 beta 36

  • The sessions list opens to the card's right (below it at the screen's edge), and the queue moves out of its way.

Aki 0.3.3

Fixes that matter

  • Marks could go to the wrong conversation. Session names came from a copy of Orca's tab names that Orca stopped updating, so an old name showed on a conversation that is now another one. Names now come only from Orca's live list, and marking opens on the session you chose last.
  • Updates never restart Aki while marks wait to be sent: it downloads, waits for the queue, then restarts. Checking only shows what's new; installing is always a click.
  • Orca's own pop-ups (and anything over its terminals) can be marked.

Smoother

  • The tag over what you point at says "↑ bigger · ↓ smaller": ↑ takes the block, the whole terminal, the window.
  • The History shows the queue in its own block on top; "See the queue" in the menu bar pin's menu; esc closes the History.
  • One six-dot handle wherever something can be dragged; the queue's destination reads as a chooser and the button says "Send".
  • The sidebar's resize corner and pointer stay right; the rings show just the number of waiting marks.
  • The update's progress also shows in the menu bar pin's menu and in Settings.

Aki 0.3.2

Updates, like they should be

  • A new version shows as a pill by the sidebar. Click it and it downloads right there — a bar filling up, Aki's pin riding its tip — then Aki restarts by itself on the new version and says so. No more update windows.
  • Aki looks for a new version every hour.

Marking

  • The comment card can be dragged by its top, off what you want to see.
  • The queue's destination is a clear field: the AI, the app and the session's whole name.

Privacy, said plainly

  • Aki sends anonymous notices to its maker when it's installed and when it updates: its version (and the one before), your macOS version and language. No account, no identifier, nothing you mark. They tell how many people use Aki and on which version, so the right things get fixed first. Get started says so, and one switch turns them off (also in Settings → General → Privacy).
